business_ops.seasonality: "Our Company's business is inherently seasonal in nature, with the installation of wind turbine towers at project sites being significantly impacted during the monsoon/rainy season due to unfavourable weather conditions and related logistical constraints. Such conditions often cause delays in project execution during the April-September period, which in turn impacts the demand for our towers and results in comparatively lower sales during this period. Consequently, our revenues and profitability tend to be lower in the monsoon season and higher during periods of favourable weather conditions." Half yearly sales turnover (Rs. in lakhs): April-September 4,137.16 (28.88%) in 2025-26, 1,553.72 (19.77%) in 2024-25, 1,595.19 (29.50%) in 2023-24; October-March 10,189.54 (71.12%) in 2025-26, 6,305.14 (80.23%) in 2024-25, 3,811.45 (70.50%) in 2023-24. Combined with cyclical variations in the renewable energy industry, this may lead to considerable fluctuations in financial performance across quarters or half-yearly periods.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Client-supplied material / conversion (job-work style) model on the tower line: the business process is Order Confirmation, then "Client Supplies Materials" - "The client supplies essential raw materials such as plates, flanges, internal weldable parts, internal assemblies, door frames, and paint" - followed by material matching and verification, production, final checklist and inspection in the presence of a client representative, issue of a Work Completion Certificate, invoicing and Delivery (Ex-Works) where the client or their designated logistics partner arranges pickup from the company premises. Manufacturing is in-house and fully integrated on-site across 22 stages (CNC cutting, beveling, rolling, longitudinal seam welding, re-rolling, ultrasonic testing, flange fitting, can-to-can fitting, weld inspection inside/outside, full-section UT, bush fit-up and welding, door fit-up and welding, ring flange bracket, surface blasting, primer coating, final paint/PU coating, orange marking, client logo application and final assembly), with all plant and machinery fully owned by the company and an in-house laboratory and testing equipment. "The in-house manufacturing operations enable us to stream line inventory management and production process resulting into maintenance of high-quality production standards, minimizing production time and bringing cost effectiveness." Raw materials are primarily Mild Steel (M.S.) plates plus shots and grits, paint, welding rods, electric plasma power sources for cutting, oxy-fuel stations, grinding wheels, ladders, lightning protection systems and platforms; "All raw materials are procured domestically from local suppliers" - geographical classification of raw material procured shows Imported Goods of Rs. 20.98 lakhs (0.25%) in FY 31-03-2026 versus Indigenous Goods Rs. 8,371.08 lakhs (99.75%), and nil imports in FY 31-03-2025 and FY 31-03-2024. Cost of raw material consumed was Rs 4,731.58 lakhs, Rs 2,500.72 lakhs and Rs. 1,915.92 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024. State-wise raw material procurement is concentrated in Gujarat (74.03% / 32.72% / 67.65%), Karnataka (15.46% / 31.16% / 9.71%) and Maharashtra (8.52% / 33.21% / 11.89%) for 31-03-2026 / 31-03-2025 / 31-03-2024. Logistics: "The transportation of steel plates and other raw materials to the manufacturing facility, as well as the delivery of finished goods to customers, is generally arranged by the respective suppliers and customers. Accordingly, the Company does not have any dedicated logistics arrangements for these activities." The Company engages a logistics service provider for sending semi-finished goods for job work and receiving them after processing, and for transporting finished goods from the manufacturing facility to the storage area, and owns one vehicle used for minor logistics and internal transportation. Collaboration: "Our Company has so far not entered into any technical and financial collaboration agreement with the third party." No long-term supply arrangements with suppliers and no long-term agreements with customers.

overview.business_model: The Company fabricates windmill towers as tubular steel structures made of multiple cylindrical sections (commonly five per tower), rolled from heavy Mild Steel (M.S.) plates, longitudinally and circumferentially welded and joined through flanges and bolts during erection at the project site; sections are transported by road to the project site. It sells to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of Wind Turbine Generators ("WTG") and companies in the renewable energy sector. Revenue is reported as Tower Manufacturing and fabrication (Rs. 13,518.76 lakhs in FY 31-03-2026), Boiler Accessories & Paper machinery parts (Rs. 18.00 lakhs) and Others, being sale of weldmash / scrap (Rs. 789.93 lakhs). Raw materials (M.S. plates, shots and grits, paint, welding rods, ladders, lightning protection systems, platforms, etc.) are primarily sourced from local suppliers in India; cost of goods sold was Rs. 4,528.29 lakhs, Rs. 2,365.07 lakhs and Rs. 1,116.48 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024, representing 30.09%, 20.65% and 38.81% of revenue from operations.

genesis.founding_story: Ayush Nimish Vashi and Bhavin Navinchandra Desai were the initial subscribers to the Memorandum of Association, subscribing 50,000 Equity Shares each. The Company commenced operations pursuant to a declaration for commencement of business dated April 19, 2021 filed with the Registrar of Companies, Ahmedabad, and commenced commercial operations in April 2021 initially focusing on fabrication of weldmesh and assembly of boiler accessories and paper machinery parts. Building on that foundation and leveraging its expertise in steel fabrication, it strategically shifted into the wind energy sector in 2023 and has since focused on manufacturing fabrication components for wind turbine towers. The Company is led by Promoters and Executive Directors Nimish Kumar Rameshchandra Vashi (Chairman & Managing Director, associated with the Company since February, 2025) and Ayush Nimish Vashi (Whole-Time Director, associated since incorporation).

The offer buys no growth: the only quantified object is Rs 11,500.00 lakhs of borrowing repayment plus an unquantified general corporate purpose - project.total_cost_lakhs is null, there is no capex object, no machinery or quotation annexure, and no funding mix. The Rs 13,00,800-share Offer for Sale by Nimish Kumar Rameshchandra Vashi brings no proceeds to the Company at all.

Leverage was built hard and fast right before the offer: total outstanding indebtedness Rs 12,824.76 lakhs at March 31, 2026 (secured portion Rs 12,308 lakhs) against net worth of Rs 8,951.16 lakhs; FY26 financing inflow of Rs 8,030.36 lakhs included Rs 9,029.27 lakhs of fresh long-term borrowing against only Rs 2,030.05 lakhs repaid, and all fund-based facilities sit with a single lender, Bank of Baroda. Rs 516.76 lakhs of unsecured loans (4.03% of total indebtedness) are recallable at any time.

The newly commissioned capacity is barely running: Kutch Unit-II utilisation is 8.04% in FY26 (actual production 4,822.20 MT in its single operating month, March 2026) and Karnataka 41.74%; company-level tower utilisation is 48.17%. Under-utilisation is itself a high-severity risk factor in the DRHP.

Governance turnover is unexplained: both independent directors appointed April 1, 2025 - Balwant Pooranmal Tayal and Navin Kumar Kewalchand Bhurat - resigned with effect from June 19, 2025, with no reason recorded, and replacements were appointed w.e.f. June 20, 2025. No director has previously served on the board of a listed company, and committee memberships are not populated in the extract.

Related-party density is high: 75 related-party transaction lines. Promoter/MD Nimish Vashi took loans of Rs 1,442.24 lakhs in FY26 (repaid Rs 1,039.58 lakhs); group company Darpan Infrastructure Private Limited lent Rs 1,389.52 lakhs (FY24) and Rs 1,018.67 lakhs (FY25), charged Rs 97.60 lakhs as commission for a corporate guarantee in FY26, is the landlord of the registered office, and until November 30, 2023 held 51% of the Company before transferring control to the promoter. Darpan's own financials are not set out in the DRHP.

Concentration on every axis, with no long-term contracts on either side: top-1 customer 29.32% and top-5 78.75% of FY26 revenue; top-10 suppliers 90.11% of FY26 purchases (up from 72.44% in FY24); Karnataka 93.87% of FY26 revenue; Tower Manufacturing and Fabrication 94.36% of FY26 revenue. Working capital absorbs the profit: inventory days 252.85 / 175.06 / 202.69 (FY26/FY25/FY24); inventories rose to Rs 5,068.78 lakhs from Rs 1,205.01 lakhs and trade receivables to Rs 3,894.54 lakhs from Rs 2,516.61 lakhs, so FY26 CFO of Rs 1,843.94 lakhs converts only about half of the Rs 3,662.83 lakhs PAT. Debtor days, creditor days and the cash conversion cycle are blank in the source and trade payables are null for all three years.

Corporate-records hygiene is weak and graded high severity by the extraction: clerical errors in PAS-3 filings, inaccuracies in the altered MOA, incorrect first-financial-year details and incorrect figures in passed resolutions; past board reports omitted disclosure of funds accepted from directors/relatives and the CSR report; BEN-2 filed late; DPT-3 filed with clerical mistakes that cannot be revised; 14 delayed ROC forms across FY2021-22 to FY2025-26 (delay-days column not populated in the source).

Property and title are unresolved at both sites: certain Kutch properties were acquired from a seller not in possession of the original registered title deeds, reported lost (FIR dated October 11, 2021, Anjar Police Station; sale agreement dated October 14, 2021); the registered office is rented from group company Darpan at Rs 5,000 per month; and 19 open storage plots at Koppal are on third-party rent with 'no activity being carried out on any of these plots'. Both independent directors appointed April 1, 2025 (Balwant Pooranmal Tayal, Navin Kumar Kewalchand Bhurat) resigned with effect from June 19, 2025 - inside 80 days, with no reason disclosed - immediately before the pre-IPO placements and the offer.

Manufacturing unit 2 at Kutch - the Rs 60,000 MTPA plant just commissioned - carries no insurance policy, alongside no workmen, product-liability or keyman cover.
